learn.title: A rule for right triangles
learn.body: In a right triangle the two sides that meet at the right angle are the legs. The side across from the right angle, and the longest one, is the hypotenuse. One equation connects all three sides.

learn.title: The theorem
learn.body: If the legs are $a$ and $b$ and the hypotenuse is $c$, then $a^2+b^2=c^2$. The triangle shown has legs 3 and 4: $9+16=25$, so $c=5$. It works only for right triangles.
learn.alt: A right triangle with a short vertical leg labelled a equals 3, a horizontal leg labelled b equals 4, and the slanted side labelled c.

learn.title: The converse
learn.body: If the sides of a triangle satisfy $a^2+b^2=c^2$ with $c$ the longest, then the triangle is a right triangle. Test $7,24,25$: $49+576=625=25^2$. Yes, it is a right triangle.
Add the squares of the legs to find the hypotenuse. Subtract to find a leg. The hypotenuse is always the longest side.

questions.explanation: The wall and ground form the legs: $h^2=100-36=64$, so $h=8$.
